record_identity.title: Anthropic reported Moonshot and DeepSeek routed customer conversations through Claude for distillation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 2026 Moonshot and DeepSeek customer-conversation routing and distillation campaigns
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report states that Moonshot activity attributable to the campaign occurred between May and July 2026 and that the DeepSeek campaign included more than 12.1 million exchanges over 14 days in July 2026. The range is an occurrence envelope rather than an assertion of continuous activity.

summary: Anthropic reported that Moonshot AI and DeepSeek silently routed real customer requests through Claude and used resulting exchanges in model-distillation and training workflows. Anthropic states that Moonshot users believed they were using Kimi while receiving Claude responses, that Moonshot saved at least part of the relayed exchanges for training, and that DeepSeek similarly relayed selected customer requests to Claude without informing customers. Anthropic reported more than 23 million Moonshot-attributable exchanges between May and July 2026 and more than 12.1 million DeepSeek-attributable exchanges over 14 days in July, with some routed material containing sensitive customer or organisational information. VIGIL classifies the occurrence primarily as Secondary-Purpose Authority Transposition because information supplied for service delivery was repurposed into a materially different model-development pathway, and secondarily as Industrial-Scale Unauthorised Capability Extraction because customer traffic was used at campaign scale to acquire and transfer Claude capabilities into downstream training workflows. These classifications preserve Anthropic's attribution as an investigated provider claim and do not independently determine legal liability or the affected users' jurisdictions.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report directly describes separate Moonshot and DeepSeek campaigns. For Moonshot, Anthropic states that customer requests were silently forwarded to Claude rather than processed by Kimi, Claude responses were shown to users, at least some exchanges were captured and saved, and extracted Claude reasoning traces were used for model training. For DeepSeek, Anthropic states that selected user requests were silently relayed to Claude and that the resulting reasoning traces were extracted for downstream distillation. Anthropic reports more than 23 million exchanges attributable to Moonshot between May and July 2026 and more than 12.1 million exchanges attributable to DeepSeek over 14 days in July. Reuters, The Wall Street Journal and the South China Morning Post independently report Anthropic's findings concerning live customer-query routing and sensitive information. The available public evidence does not identify individual affected users or establish their jurisdictions, and VIGIL does not treat Anthropic's provider attribution as an independently adjudicated legal finding.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Two distinct governance mechanisms are evidenced by the reported conduct. First, customer communications supplied for the primary purpose of obtaining service from Kimi or DeepSeek were redirected into Claude interactions and then used in a materially different training, distillation or capability-extraction purpose. Authority to process information for service delivery does not by itself establish authority to repurpose that information for external model interaction and downstream model development; this maps to FC-000055 Secondary-Purpose Authority Transposition. Second, the routing occurred as part of systematic high-volume campaigns designed to extract Claude capabilities for downstream training. The scale, repeated access pathways, concealment and training purpose satisfy the distinct FC-000068 Industrial-Scale Unauthorised Capability Extraction mechanism. The silent substitution of Claude for the model customers believed they were using is also governance-significant because it obscures the actual processing chain, but VIGIL does not force that disclosure problem into a separate class where the current taxonomy does not provide a cleaner occurrence-level fit.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates that model routing is not merely infrastructure metadata. A user-facing model identity can conceal a materially different processing chain in which user content crosses providers and becomes input to model development. Governance therefore needs purpose-bound authority, routing provenance and user-facing disclosure sufficient to distinguish which model actually processed information, whether information was relayed to another provider, and whether it entered a training or distillation pathway. The case also shows that secondary-purpose data use and industrial-scale model extraction can co-occur without being collapsed into one mechanism.
assessment_boundaries: The occurrence is reported and attributed by Anthropic; VIGIL does not independently adjudicate the named firms' legal liability or contractual breach.
Reuters, The Wall Street Journal and the South China Morning Post independently report Anthropic's findings but do not independently reproduce Anthropic's underlying traffic telemetry.
VIGIL does not assert that Australian personal information was among the routed conversations; the reviewed public evidence does not identify affected users by nationality or residence.
Sensitive-data examples are attributed only where Anthropic allocates them to a named campaign; broad reporting about sensitive routed data is not redistributed between firms without source support.

FC-000055 classifies the reported repurposing of service-delivery data into a materially different model-development purpose; it does not imply that all model routing or all distillation is unauthorised.
FC-000068 classifies the reported industrial-scale capability-extraction campaign; legitimate distillation undertaken with valid authority remains outside the class.
The model-substitution and disclosure issue is recorded as a governance finding but is not assigned an additional taxonomy class absent a cleaner current fit.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Resolve Anthropic's first-party occurrence wording into the distinct purpose-authority and industrial-scale capability-extraction mechanisms while preserving provider-attribution and legal-liability boundaries.

clauses.source_anchor: silently forwarded customer requests to Claude
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Authority to receive customer information for one service does not itself authorise forwarding that information to a different model provider for a materially different processing chain.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The source describes customer-supplied information moving from the service-delivery purpose into an undisclosed external-model pathway without an independently established secondary-purpose authority basis.

clauses.source_anchor: captured and saved at least a portion of these exchanges
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Information collected to answer a customer's request does not acquire training or model-development authority merely because the service can retain or technically reuse the exchange.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Saving relayed customer exchanges for downstream training is the materially different secondary purpose protected by FC-000055.

clauses.source_anchor: silently relayed exchanges to Claude without informing DeepSeek customers
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A customer-facing service must not treat access to customer content as sufficient authority to route that content through a different provider and processing purpose without an adequate authority or governance basis.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The source expressly connects undisclosed cross-provider routing to the same customer-data secondary-purpose mechanism.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Repeated, distributed model access must be assessed cumulatively when it is used to acquire upstream capabilities for downstream training; per-request access does not automatically create authority for industrial-scale capability extraction.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic reports a systematic campaign operating at tens of millions of exchanges and expressly links harvested outputs and reasoning traces to downstream training and distillation.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Anthropic's directly reviewed September 2026 report describes live customer communications being silently routed through Claude and reused in downstream training/distillation workflows, while also describing systematic campaigns at industrial scale. The occurrence therefore maps primarily to VIGIL-FC-000055 Secondary-Purpose Authority Transposition and secondarily to VIGIL-FC-000068 Industrial-Scale Unauthorised Capability Extraction. Classification expresses the mechanisms in the reported occurrence and does not independently adjudicate legal liability.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Customer-supplied information provided to obtain an AI service response was reportedly repurposed into an undisclosed external-model interaction and downstream training/distillation pathway without an independently established secondary-purpose authority basis.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: Anthropic reports repeated, concealed and distributed campaigns at tens of millions of exchanges in which Claude outputs and reasoning traces were harvested for downstream model training, satisfying the industrial-scale capability-extraction mechanism.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All eleven dimensions were retained or re-reviewed against the strengthened first-party occurrence evidence. The evidence supports S4 privacy/confidentiality harm through large-scale cross-provider exposure of customer communications, including highly sensitive information. Other dimensions remain unreported unless specifically assessed and do not lower or raise the derived result.

observed_values.qualitative_value: Anthropic reports real customer traffic routed across providers at campaign scale, including sensitive individual, corporate and government-related information.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Anthropic reports that Moonshot and DeepSeek routed real customer requests through Claude without customer awareness and that some routed material contained highly sensitive customer or organisational information. The campaigns operated at large scale, and independent reporting corroborates the reported cross-provider routing and sensitive-data exposure. This supports the S4 threshold for large-scale or highly sensitive exposure and substantial evidenced misuse. The assessment does not identify affected individuals or infer jurisdictions not established by the sources.
